items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer asks 'did you work with Curtin' but the interviewee does not respond to this specific question, instead discussing McKinney's Cotton Pickers and Curtis Moseby. No direct interaction or relationship with 'Curtin' is described by the interviewee.

ctx.x: Yeah, but if I don't find a person that actually is sincere, and actually wants to do it, I won't bother with them at all. But by the same token, you find that sometimes a person has to pay for what they do before they will appreciate it, because a lot of times you give things for free and it's not appreciated. If you put a monetary value on it, then they will feel as though they've got to learn it, because they're paying for it, which is strictly a bad turnaround.
